questions.question: Of which of the following Pratihara kings was Rajashekhara, the famous poet and dramatist, the court poet?
questions.solution:
Mahendrapala (885-910 AD)
Works of Rajshekhara: Vidhdashalabhanjika, Balabharata, Karpuramanjari, Balaramayana, Kavyamimamsa.
Gurjara Pratihara dynasty (8th to 11th century):
  • Founder - Harichandra
  • Mihira Bhoja (836-885 AD) - Most powerful Pratihara king
  • Yashpala (1024-1036) - last ruler of the Gurjara Pratihara dynasty

questions.question: Who were the first to make land grants to Brahmins?
questions.solution:
Satavahanas (1st Century BC to 3rd Century AD)
  • Simuka was the founder of Satavahana dynasty
  • Sakas (2nd century BCE to the 4th century CE) - The most famous Shaka ruler in India was Rudradaman (130 AD to 150 AD); came to an end with the defeat of the last Shaka ruler, Rudrasimha III by Chandragupta II (Gupta dynasty)
  • Kushans (First-Third Centuries) - Founded by Kujula Kadphises

questions.question: During the reign of which of the following Pallavas, Hiuen Tsang visited the Pallava capital Kanchi?
questions.solution:
Narasimhavarman I
He was also known as Mahamalla or Mamalla, which means "great wrestler". He took the title Vatapikonda (the conqueror of Vatapi).

questions.question: The Rampurva bull that was part of a Mauryan pillar found in Rampurva, Bihar is now placed at
questions.solution:
Rashtrapati Bhavan
The Pillars of Ashoka are the most famous examples of Mauryan art. The Rashtrapati Bhavan houses the imposing 3rd century BC Ashoka pillar of sandstone known as the Rampurva bull. It got its name from the place of its discovery, Rampurva in Bihar.

questions.question: Who among the following was the last Pallava king?
questions.solution:
Aparajitavarman
Pallava dynasty (275 CE to 897 CE) - Also known as Tondaimandalam.
  • Founder - Simha Vishnu (Avanisimha)
  • Mahendravarman - He defeated the Kalabhras and re-established the Pallava kingdom
  • Narasimhavarman I - Son of Mahendravarman

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about Kandariya Mahadeva Temple:
Statement 1: Kandariya Mahadeva Temple at Khajuraho was built in 999 A.D. by King Dhangadeva of the Chandela dynasty.
Statement 2: Kandariya Mahadeva Temple was constructed in Tamil Nadu under the Chola dynasty in Dravida style.
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is true, but Statement 2 is false
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is false, but Statement 2 is true
questions.solution:
Statement 1 is true, but Statement 2 is false
Kandariya Mahadeva temple was built at Khajuraho (Madhya Pradesh), made up of sandstone. Its first mention is found in 'al Biruni' and 'Ibn Battuta' work. It follows the Nagara Style of architecture and was recognized by UNESCO as a world heritage site in 1986.
Other temples built by Chandela dynasty (Founder - Nanuka): Devi Jagadamba Temple, Chitragupta Temple, Laxmana Temple.

questions.question: In the mid-eighth century, Dantidurga, a Rashtrakuta chief, overthrew his Chalukya overlord and performed a ritual literally called a
questions.solution:
Golden womb (Hiranyagarbha)
This ritual was performed with the help of Brahmanas; it was thought to lead to the "rebirth" of the sacrificer as a Kshatriya, even if he was not one by birth. The first known ruler of the dynasty was Dantidurga who conquered Badami in 752 A.D., defeating the Chalukyas.

questions.question: The emblem of the Chera Dynasty that controlled the central and northern parts of Kerala and the Kongu region of Tamil Nadu was
questions.solution:
Bow and Arrow
The symbol also appears on the coins the dynasty minted. The dynasty controlled the central and northern parts of Kerala and the Kongu region of Tamil Nadu. Their capital was Vanji, Tamil Nadu.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT part of six schools of Indian Philosophy?
questions.solution:
Dravida
The six orthodox schools (darshanas) of Indian philosophy are:
  • Samkhya - Founded by Kapila (Book - Samkhya sutra); holds that reality is constituted of two principles: Prakriti (female) and Purusha (male)
  • Yoga - Union of the two principal entities
  • Nyaya - A technique of logical thinking; author of Nyaya Sutras - Gautama
  • Vaisheshika
  • Mimamsa
  • Vedanta

questions.question: The Amaravati School of art was developed under the patronage of
questions.solution:
Satavahanas
Different Schools of art:
  • Gandhara School of Art (Kushana) - Developed in the North West Frontier, in the modern-day Kandahar region
  • Mathura School of Art (Kushana) - Developed around Mathura
  • Amaravati School of Art (Satavahanas) - Developed in the Andhra region

questions.question: Who among the following was a famous ruler of the Pandya dynasty of South India?
questions.solution:
Nedunjeliyan II
He was made 'Pandya supreme in the south'. He defeated a confederacy of the Cholas and Cheras at Talayilanganam near Tiruvarur. His deeds have been described in the Maduraikkanci.
Pandya Empire - Established by King Kadungon in the 6th century AD. Capitals - Korkai, Madurai.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Sangam period:
1. The Tamil word Muvendar in Sangam poems refers to the three ruling chiefs - the Cholas, the Cheras, and the Pandyas.
2. The term Muvendar was used for the three great ports of ancient Tamilakam.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
1 only
Muvendar literally means "three chiefs," referring to Cholas, Cheras, and Pandyas.

questions.question: The term 'Kammakaras' in ancient times is related to
questions.solution:
Landless agricultural labourers
Terminologies related in ancient times:
  • Shrenis - In ancient times, crafts persons and merchants formed associations
  • Samaharta and Sannidata - Tax collecting officers in ancient times
  • Sonalika - A Sanskrit word that refers to a goldsmith
  • Grihapati - Independent farmers
  • Agrahara - Land granted to a Brahmana
  • Kammakaras - Landless agricultural labourers

questions.question: Who among the following gave up his traditional professions and took to arms, successfully established a kingdom in Karnataka?
questions.solution:
Kadamba Mayurasharman
He was a Brahmana. The Kadamba Mayurasharman (345-365 C.E.) was the founder of the Kadamba Kingdom of Banavasi (Karnataka). Kadimi Chettu (story of Mayur Sharma) was written by Visawanatha Satyanarayana (Padma Bhushan (1970), Jnanpith Award (1971)).

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about Ravikirti:
Statement 1: Ravikirti, a Jain poet, was the court poet of Pulakeshin II of the Chalukya dynasty of Vatapi.
Statement 2: Ravikirti's famous inscription in honour of his patron king is found at the Meguti Jain Temple in Aihole, Karnataka.
questions.option_3: Statement 1 is true, but Statement 2 is false
questions.option_4: Statement 1 is false, but Statement 2 is true
questions.solution:
Both statements are true
The Jain poet Ravikirti was the court poet of Pulakeshin II (610 to 642 CE), the first sovereign ruler of the Chalukya dynasty of Vatapi (modern Badami). Ravikirti's Aihole inscription (a nineteen-line Sanskrit inscription), in honour of his patron king, is found in the Meguti Jain temple at Aihole, Karnataka.
Dynasties:
  • Chalukya dynasty (between 6th and 12th centuries)
  • Pallava dynasty (275 CE to 897 CE)
  • Chera dynasty (in the Sangam period and before)
  • Chola dynasty (300 BCE to 1279 CE)

questions.question: Who among the following was the founder of the Kanva dynasty?
questions.solution:
Vasudeva Kanva (73-63 BCE)
He founded the Kanva dynasty (72-28 BCE, Kanvayanas).
Rulers of the Kanva dynasty: Bhumimitra (64-50 BCE), Narayana (50-38 BCE), Susarman (38-28 BCE).
  • Capital: Pataliputra
  • Devabhuti - the last ruler of the Shunga Dynasty

questions.question: The rulers of which of the following dynasties built the Khajuraho temples between 950 to 1050 A.D in central India?
questions.solution:
Chandela Dynasty
The Khajuraho Group of Monuments are a group of Hindu and Jain temples in Chhatarpur district, Madhya Pradesh, known for their erotic sculpture. The Pratiharas, also known as the Gurjara-Pratiharas (Founder - Harichandra). The most well-known king of the Pratihara dynasty was Bhoja or Mihira Bhoja.

questions.question: In which of the following languages did Amoghavarsha write Kavirajamarga?
questions.solution:
Kannada
Amoghavarsha (Rashtrakuta ruler) also wrote 'Prasnottara Ratna Malika' (Sanskrit). He patronized many Indian scholars including mathematician Mahaviracharya, who wrote Ganita-sara-samgraha, Jinasena, Virasena, Shakatayan, and Sri Vijaya (a Kannada language theorist). He held titles such as Nrupathunga, Atishadhvala, Veeranarayana, Rattamarthanda, and Srivallabha during his reign. Historian Panchamukhi called him the 'Ashoka of South'.

questions.question: Which king of the Pala dynasty defeated Indrayudh and made Chakrayudha as the ruler of Kannauj?
questions.solution:
Dharmapala (770-810)
He founded the Vikramshila University (Bhagalpur, Bihar) and built Somapuri monastery, Bihar. In 750 AD, Gopala founded the Pala dynasty. Capital: Muddagiri/Munger (Bihar).

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Mukteshwara Temple, a 10th-century temple dedicated to Lord Shiva.
2. The Sun Temple of Konark was built by Narasimhadeva I.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
Both 1 and 2
The Mukteshwara Temple is a 10th-century Shiva temple in Bhubaneswar, Odisha, known as the 'Gem of Odisha architecture.' The Sun Temple at Konark was built in the 13th century by Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty.

questions.question: Queen Rudramadevi belonged to which dynasty of India?
questions.solution:
Kakatiya
Marco Polo mentioned her in his writings. Rudradeva I was the first independent ruler of this kingdom of Warangal. Their capital was Orugallu, now known as Warangal. In 1323, Prince Jaunakhan (Muhammad bin Tughlaq) defeated Prataparudra Deva (the last ruler of this kingdom) and annexed their kingdom.

questions.question: Which place had a water harvesting system channeling the flood water of the Ganga river in the first century B.C.?
questions.solution:
Sringaverapura (near Allahabad in Uttar Pradesh)
Water harvesting in India:
  • Dholavira in Harappan civilization
  • Bhopal Lake (built by the Paramara Raja Bhoj in 11th century)
  • Iltutmish constructed a tank in Hauz Khas for supplying water to the Siri Fort (14th century)

questions.question: Which state of India was ruled by the Ningthouja dynasty?
questions.solution:
Manipur
It has 125 extended families. It was apparently founded by King Nongda Lairen Pakhangba in 33 CE.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Elephanta Caves:
1. The Elephanta Caves, located on Elephanta Island (Gharapuri) in Mumbai Harbour, were declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987.
2. These caves, predominantly dedicated to Lord Vishnu, were built by the Rashtrakuta rulers.
3. The total number of caves at Elephanta is around 34.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
1 and 3 only
The Elephanta Caves are dedicated mainly to Lord Shiva, not Lord Vishnu. They are on Elephanta Island near Mumbai, declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987, with about 34 caves.

questions.question: In which of the following temples will you find Gopurams?
questions.solution:
Shiva Temple, Chidambaram
A gopuram or gopura is a monumental tower, usually ornate, at the entrance of any temple, especially in Southern India. They are a prominent feature of koils, Hindu temples built in the Dravidian style. They are topped by the kalasam, a bulbous stone finial. Nataraja temple in Chidambaram, Tamil Nadu is one of the famous examples of Gopuram.

questions.question: Who among the following wrote the basic text of Vaisheshika philosophy?
questions.solution:
Kanada
It is an ancient Sanskrit text at the foundation of the Vaisheshika school of Hindu philosophy. Vaisheshika is one of the six classical schools of Indian philosophy, often referred to as "Darshanas."

questions.question: Yashovigraha, Mahichandra and Chandradeva were the first three rulers of ______ dynasty.
questions.solution:
Gahadavala
Yashovigraha was the founder of the Gahadavala dynasty. The majority of the Gahadavala epigraphic records were discovered in Uttar Pradesh.

questions.question: In which of the following caves is the painting named 'Padmapani Bodhisattva' found?
questions.solution:
Ajanta Cave No. 1
The iconic Ajanta paintings Padmapani and Vajrapani glorify the walls of Cave 1 of Ajanta. Cave 1 of Ajanta was built in the second phase of excavation under the patronage of King Harisena of the Vakataka dynasty.

questions.question: Kolathunadu, Valluvanad and Thekkumkoor were ancient small-time kingdoms in which state of India?
questions.solution:
Kerala
  • Kolathunadu - land lying between Perumba river in the north and Putupattanam river in the south
  • Valluvanad (Founder - Ilayi Raja) - Region between Meenachil and Pamban rivers
  • Thekkumkoor - The region between the Nila river and Panthaloor Hills
